::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Which manuals are on your "TeX Reference" shelf?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/66/which-manuals-are-on-your-tex-reference-shelf), asked by [Sharpie](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/17/sharpie) on TeX Stack Exchange (2010-07-26; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> This is a community wiki since there is no "one true answer"- if you find an answer that contains a lot of your choices, but is missing something you feel is incredibly useful.  Feel free to add it.  A short description of what topics the reference covers would be nice as well.
>
> Organize by subject please.
>
> For example: I always keep the following PDFs at my fingertips.
>
> ### Document Layout
>
>   * [The Memoir manual](http://www.ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/memoir/):  Covers, in exquisite detail, how to produce just about any document using the `memoir` LaTeX class. ([PDF](http://tug.ctan.org/tex-archive/macros/latex/contrib/memoir/memman.pdf) 4.5 MB)
>
> ### Mathematical Typesetting
>
>   * [Math Mode](http://tug.ctan.org/obsolete/info/math/voss/mathmode/): A document by Herbert Voß that explains how to typeset just about any mathematical expression in LaTeX. ([PDF](http://tug.ctan.org/obsolete/info/math/voss/mathmode/Mathmode.pdf) 2 MB)
>
> ### Graphics
>
>   * [The PGF Manual](https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf): Explains, with examples, how to draw just about any figure using PGF/TikZ.  Also a good example of what awesome documentation should look like. ([PDF](http://mirror.macomnet.net/pub/CTAN/graphics/pgf/base/doc/pgfmanual.pdf) 9.5 MB)
:::

At work I have the beamer and pgf manuals open about 50% of the time.  *The TeXbook* is one of the most thumbed books I own.  But I also would like to recommend *[A Guide to LaTeX](http://www.amazon.com/Guide-LATEX-Document-Preparation-Beginners/dp/0201398257)* by Kopka and Daly.  A very nice guide that starts from basics and ends with a bit of programming.
